explanation: Inverters are configured to momentarily cease current injection when voltages fall outside the 0.9–1.1 pu continuous operating range.
When voltage drops below 0.9 pu, control logic freezes to prevent controller windup and inverters enter cessation or ride-through mode.
Once voltage recovers to within the continuous operating range, inverters resume responding to plant-level controller commands.
BAs specify ramp rate limits to prevent excessive power output changes during normal operation.
Generators must provide reactive power proportional to active power output (33% of active power) to maintain power factor requirements at all output levels.
Reactive power capability at zero active power output may be less than 100% due to hardware, software, or design limitations.
IEEE Std 1547-2018 does not require reactive power capability for active power output less than 5 percent.

explanation: Excessive negative sequence current can damage capacitors and other electrical components in the system.
Instantaneous tripping should not be used unless reverse current exceeds inverter or PV module ratings to avoid unnecessary tripping during transient conditions.

explanation: High-resolution point-on-wave data (≥960 samples per second) is required for accurate monitoring of bus voltage phase quantities.

explanation: Droop must remain proportional to Pmax/Pmin to ensure consistent frequency response across operational ranges.
